clue.text: Lie in bed, poorly — it's impossible to get down

indicators.note: poorly suggests the words are in a bad way, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lying in bed feeling unwell finds the food can't be swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' rearranges LIEINBED; 'get down' here means swallow, not descend.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that cannot be swallowed or eaten safely is described as not fit for eating.

clue.text: End of chase, heading off people on horses — we get down from them

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so the last letter of chase is taken
losing the heading means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: people on horses are riders

explanation.surface: At the end of a hunt, riders lead the way and dismount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' is not dismounting but feathers: eider ducks give eiderdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Eider ducks are the source of soft down feathers used in quilts and pillows.

clue.text: Person who agrees with fool put down

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to enter something is to put it down in writing, as in a register

explanation.surface: Someone who agrees with an idiot is snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' looks like an insult but means record in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: One who gives assent, consenting to a proposal, is a person who agrees.

clue.text: About employer who makes things go down in America?

definitions.text: who makes things go down in America?

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about
one who employs or makes use of something is a user

explanation.surface: A question about a boss who makes American things fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go down' is American slang for happen ('what's going down'), so whoever makes things happen is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who brings events about is their originator, and in US slang events 'go down' when they happen.

clue.text: Improvise as supplier of a cross, exactly what's needed

parts.note: in football the wing is the position from which crosses are delivered into the box
IT means just the thing, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: A winger delivering crosses is exactly what the team needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' is a football pass from the side of the pitch, not anger or the shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To wing it is an idiom for acting without preparation, making things up as you go.

clue.text: Perturbed re snow, go downhill

indicators.note: perturbed means agitated or disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Bothered by snow, a skier heads down the slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perturbed' rearranges RESNOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To go downhill is an idiom for deteriorating, getting steadily worse.

clue.text: Varied across goals achieved by top players

indicators.note: varied means changed about, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Top footballers score various goals all over the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Varied' rearranges ACROSS; the 'players' are actors, not sportsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Academy Awards are the prizes leading film actors aim to win.

clue.text: Observe, in present and past, move up and down

parts.note: observe in the present tense is see
the verb observe, see, in the past tense is saw

explanation.surface: Watching the present and the past, the mind swings back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'past' borrows 'Observe' from the first part: the past tense of see.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground plank pivoting in the middle rocks its riders up and down, and the verb describes that motion.

clue.text: Drink with Irish patron in Ulster town

parts.note: to down a drink is to drink it in one go
St Patrick is the patron saint of Ireland

explanation.surface: Having a drink with an Irish customer in a Northern Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patron' is a saint, not a pub customer. DOWNPATRICK is the county town of County Down in Northern Ireland, where Patrick is said to be buried.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a real town in the province of Northern Ireland, traditionally called Ulster.

clue.text: Go across for game

definitions.meaning: to ... a gap or river is to span it
a card game for four players

explanation.surface: Up for crossing over to play?
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to span something, and the noun is also the well-known partnership card game.

clue.text: Walk across, having finished backing favourites

parts.note: something finished is over

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A gambler crosses the street after he stops betting on the favourites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing favourites' looks like betting; 'backing' turns PETS round.
explanation.definitionFit: To step over a line or boundary is to go beyond it, literally walking across a limit.

clue.text: Kind of word that either part of down clue can be, never across

definitions.text: Kind of word that either part of down clue can be, never across

parts.words: Kind of word that either part of down clue can be, never across
parts.note: both 'down' (to swallow) and 'clue' (to inform) can be action words, but 'across' never can

explanation.surface: A grammar puzzle about the words in a crossword's headings.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the part of speech fits all three tests: 'down' and 'clue' can each be used as one, 'across' cannot.
explanation.definitionFit: A part of speech naming actions; 'down a pint' and 'clue someone in' use the words that way.

clue.text: Like some politics across the pond in programme about alliance

definitions.text: Like some politics across the pond

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the programme word goes round the alliance

parts.note: a serial is a broadcast programme in episodes
NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance

explanation.surface: American politics appears in a TV show about a military alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across the pond' is a jocular phrase for the far side of the Atlantic, here the United States, whose upper house is the Senate.
explanation.definitionFit: Politics relating to the US upper house of Congress is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Stretch over and right every thing this makes with 8

parts.note: each thing means every one, so each
this light and the one at 8 intersect in the grid, so together they form a cross

explanation.surface: Stretch over and put every item right, making something with 8.
explanation.walkthrough: The self-reference is to the grid: this entry and 8 intersect, so with it this one makes A CROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend an arm over something to get hold of it is to stretch over it.

clue.text: Down amongst them is one of the shortest company releases

parts.note: company at its shortest is the abbreviation CO
unties means releases from bonds

explanation.surface: A tiny firm's product launches feature downy goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Down is County Down in Northern Ireland, one of the Irish counties.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish administrative regions include County Down, so it is one among this group.

clue.text: Looking down on king, old hat

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after the first piece

parts.note: looking down means gloomy, which is sombre
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Gazing down on a monarch who wears an outdated hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking down' means looking gloomy, not glancing downward.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed Mexican headwear is a type of hat.

clue.text: One taking steps to provide first part of down clue's requirement, we hear

indicators.note: the first part of a word is its opening letter, so the start of down is taken
we hear means the letters come from how the word is spoken, a British non-rhotic pronunciation

parts.note: what a clue requires is an answer

explanation.surface: Someone acting to supply the start of what a down clue needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first part of' takes D from 'down'; 'we hear' turns ANSWER into ANCER, its sound in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A person performing dance moves takes steps in time to music.

clue.text: Breaking law, say, that describes how things fall down

definitions.text: that describes how things fall down

indicators.note: breaking means smashing up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Breaking the law, say, is how things collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' rearranges LAWSAY. Under gravity, things fall down every time.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropped objects fall downward every time without exception, so this adverb describes the manner.

clue.text: Moves across battlefield making me a nervous wreck

indicators.note: a wreck is something smashed up, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Troop movements on a battlefield leave a soldier shattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wreck' rearranges MEANERVOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Planned tactical movements of troops in the field are military operations of this name.

clue.text: Oddly deficient, down to last husband? Bound to be honest

indicators.note: deficient in odd letters means only the even letters remain

explanation.surface: A strangely lacking husband sinking to the last is sworn to truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly deficient' keeps the even letters of DOWNTOLAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness sworn in court is bound to tell the truth under formal promise.

clue.text: Warship went down, part of larger group

parts.note: a sub, submarine, is a warship
the sun set, meaning it went down

explanation.surface: A warship sank, a part of a bigger fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went down' suggests sinking but refers to the sun setting.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics, a collection contained within a bigger collection is called this.

clue.text: Cross made by removing ends of protective jewel

indicators.note: removing the ends means the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: an amulet is a charm worn to protect against harm

explanation.surface: An angry outburst caused by removing the edges of a lucky gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' is a hybrid, not anger: the offspring of a donkey and a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid animal bred from a male donkey and a mare is a classic example of a cross.

clue.text: Puzzle producing what sounds like a bad-tempered sign of approval

indicators.note: sounds like means the letters come from how the phrase is spoken

parts.note: bad-tempered is cross, and a sign of approval is a tick, so A CROSS TICK

explanation.surface: A puzzle gives a grumpy nod of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: A CROSS TICK said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A word puzzle in which the first letters of lines spell a word is a type of puzzle.

clue.text: 60% of bars across France produced this wine

indicators.note: sixty percent of the ten letters in these two words means only the first six are kept

explanation.surface: Most bars across France serve this wine.
explanation.walkthrough: '60% of' takes six of the ten letters of BARSACROSS, from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet white wine from Bordeaux is named after its French commune.

clue.text: More precisely, repeatedly runs across two articles

indicators.note: across means lying over, so the paired letters go around the articles

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
repeatedly asks for the runs letter a second time, so a second R stands beside the first
A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: To be exact, someone keeps running across two written pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles the runs letter, and 'across' sets that pair either side of A and THE, the two articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Used in 'or rather', the word corrects a statement to make it more exact.

clue.text: Wild animals that may be camouflaged when crossing?

definitions.text: Wild animals that may be camouflaged when crossing?

parts.words: Wild animals that may be camouflaged when crossing?
parts.note: the striped beasts share their name with a British striped road crossing, where they would blend in

explanation.surface: Wild animals hiding as they cross a road.
explanation.walkthrough: A zebra crossing is a British pedestrian crossing painted with black and white stripes.
explanation.definitionFit: Striped African wild horses would blend into a road crossing painted with the same stripes.
